subject: Request: temporary shift to quarterly invoicing and payment window
messages:
From: Tori Jensen <tori@hearthland.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, billing@hearthland.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request - temporary move to quarterly invoicing / extended payment window

Hi Sean,

Quick note from our finance team: Hearthland is implementing a treasury hold in January tied to a vendor consolidation. For Q1 and Q2 2027 they want to shift to quarterly invoicing (one invoice per quarter) and extend the payment window for those invoices to Net-90 to align with their pay cycles. PO HL-8891 is in flight but will be delayed by their internal approvals.

Can Redwood accommodate a temporary change like this for the first two quarters of 2027 while they finish procurement? They asked specifically that we try not to change pricing (no additional discount) — they just need the cadence and payment window shift.

We can provide a PO and SOW, and happy to sign an amendment. Please let me know what information you need from our side (credit info, contacts, etc.).

Thanks — Tori
Tori Jensen
Director, Procurement | Hearthland Systems
Attachments: Hearthland_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tori Jensen <tori@hearthland.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - temporary move to quarterly invoicing / extended payment window

Hi Tori — thanks for the heads up and the SOW. I’ve looped in Finance (Marissa) and Deal Desk (Karthik) to scope risk and approvals. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we can expedite:

- Do you expect the quarterly invoice to cover prior usage or only forward-looking committed spend?
- Will Hearthland be able to provide a PO for each quarter in advance, or do you need invoice-to-PO reconciliation after the fact?
- Any legal caveats from your side about amendment turnaround time?

Initial options from our side (open to alternatives):
1) Quarterly invoicing for Q1–Q2 2027, invoices issued first business day of quarter, payment Net-90. Requires an ACH authorization or refundable security deposit (one quarter’s ARR) to mitigate credit exposure.
2) Net-60 with no deposit but requires a small onboarding prepayment and regular PO issuance.

I’ll get back with a recommended path once Finance/Deal Desk weigh in. If you have a target timeline for signing the amendment, flag it and I’ll prioritize.

Best,
Sean
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - temporary move to quarterly invoicing / extended payment window (internal)

Sean — internal finance note.

Summary: Customer asks for quarterly invoices + Net-90 for two quarters (Q1/Q2 2027). Committed ARR on the SOW is ~$180k/yr (est). Risk considerations:
- Net-90 increases DSO materially; without credit protections we carry exposure for ~3 months of revenue per invoice.
- Customer is mid-market public but undergoing internal vendor consolidation (operational risk).

Recommended guardrails if we make an exception:
- Limit exception to two quarters (pilot) with automatic revert to standard monthly billing thereafter.
- Require either (A) refundable security deposit (one quarter of committed spend) OR (B) ACH autorization + approved credit check on file.
- Put invoice due date as Net-90 but include a 1.5% discount if paid within 30 days (optional incentive).
- Require PO issuance in advance of each quarter’s invoice where feasible.

See attached risk memo: Risk_Assessment_Hearthland_Q42026.pdf.

If deal desk is comfortable with no pricing changes and legal signs the amendment, I can approve this conditionally.

Marissa
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Risk_Assessment_Hearthland_Q42026.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - temporary move to quarterly invoicing / extended payment window (deal desk recommendation)

Internal — proposal for exec sign-off:

Proposal: Grant a timeboxed quarterly invoicing + Net-90 exception for Hearthland for Q1 and Q2 2027 under the following conditions:
- No change to list price (no discounting).
- Customer provides either (i) refundable security deposit equal to one quarter’s invoice OR (ii) ACH autorization + completed credit check before first invoice goes out.
- Fill out and sign our standard "Quarterly Invoicing Amendment" (attached draft).
- Limit exception to two quarters; revert to monthly billing unless both sides agree to extend via a new amendment.
- Include late fee language: 1.5% monthly on overdue balances after Net-90.

Rationale: preserves revenue and keeps the sales motion moving. Finance can accept with the deposit/ACH requirement. Legal to confirm amendment language, but I think this is within my deal desk authority to recommend to Exec.

Requesting sign-off from Markus for an exception of this nature. If approved, Sean will communicate to the customer and start a DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Deal Desk Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Quarterly_Invoicing_Amendment_Draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tori Jensen <tori@hearthland.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request - temporary move to quarterly invoicing / extended payment window

Hi Tori — thank you for your patience. Good news: Redwood is able to grant a limited exception for Hearthland for Q1 and Q2 2027 under the conditions below. We appreciate the context on your treasury timing — we’ll aim to keep this as straightforward as possible.

Approved terms (conditional):
- Quarterly invoicing for Q1 and Q2 2027 only. Invoice cadence: invoice issued on the first business day of the quarter.
- Payment terms: Net-90 from invoice date.
- Credit protection: Hearthland must either (A) provide a refundable security deposit equal to one quarter’s committed spend (refundable after Q2 if all invoices paid on time), OR (B) provide ACH authorization and complete a standard credit check before the first invoice.
- No pricing changes or discounts; we will, however, apply a 1.5% monthly late fee on balances unpaid after Net-90.
- The arrangement is contingent on a signed "Quarterly Invoicing Amendment" (DocuSign link below). Once signed and deposit/ACH is in place, we will issue the Q1 invoice.

Action items for Hearthland:
1) Sign the amendment: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-quarterly-amend
2) Provide PO or confirmation of committed spend for Q1 by Jan 5, 2027.
3) Choose payment protection option (deposit or ACH) and send details to marissa.cole@redwood.com.

If you prefer Net-60 instead of Net-90, we can discuss that route instead of a deposit. Please confirm which option you’ll take and we’ll circulate the amendment for signature.

Thanks — I’ll hold the DocuSign and coordinate with Finance to release invoices once we have the signed amendment and payment protection in place.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Quarterly_Invoicing_Amendment_Draft.pdf (pdf)
